about.heading: Mr Night (Meun Reatrey)
about.subheading: Founder, Driver and Licensed Guide · 15+ years' experience as a guide in Siem Reap · Speaks English, Thai and Khmer
story: My Cambodian name is Meun Reatrey. Reatrey means “night” in Khmer. My parents gave me this name because I was born at ten o'clock at night. So my guests call me Mr Night.

I was born and grew up in Cambodia, and my family survived the Khmer Rouge years. As a young man I trained as a Buddhist monk, and it was my dream to become one. But my father died young, so I left the monastery to work and take care of my mother.

That is how I started in tourism. For more than 15 years I have worked as a guide in Siem Reap, sharing the temples of Angkor, our villages and our Khmer culture with visitors from all over the world. Today my mother still lives with me, together with my wife Sophal and our two boys, Mony and Ratanak. Everything I earn supports my family.

Now I drive my own Toyota Alphard, with cool air-con and cold water, so you can relax between the temples. I know Siem Reap like my home, because it is my home. When you travel with me, you are not a customer, you are my guest.
Message me on WhatsApp any time. I look forward to showing you my Cambodia.

days_3d.title: Bangkok → Poipet → Siem Reap
days_3d.text: Travel Mart bus picks you up at your Bangkok hotel, then over the Poipet border and by road to Siem Reap. Hotel check-in and dinner at a local restaurant.

days_3d.title: Angkor temples with a guide
days_3d.text: Angkor Wat, Ta Prohm, Bayon and the South Gate of Angkor Thom. After lunch: the Wat Thmey killing-field memorial and Artisans d'Angkor. Free evening.

days_3d.title: Siem Reap → Bangkok
days_3d.text: The Travel Mart bus takes you from Siem Reap to Bangkok, via the Poipet border.

days_4d.title: Bangkok → Poipet → Siem Reap
days_4d.text: Travel Mart bus picks you up at your Bangkok hotel, then over the Poipet border and by road to Siem Reap. Hotel check-in and dinner at a local restaurant.

days_4d.title: Angkor temples with a guide
days_4d.text: Angkor Wat, Ta Prohm, Bayon, the South Gate of Angkor Thom, the Wat Thmey killing-field memorial and Artisans d'Angkor. Free evening.

days_4d.title: Phnom Kulen National Park
days_4d.text: Kulen Mountain, the waterfall, the River of a Thousand Lingas and the Reclining Buddha. Lunch, then shopping in the afternoon.

destinations.heading: Places I can take you
destinations.message: Hi Mr Night, I would like to visit {place}. Can you help me plan it?

items.name: Angkor Wat
items.text: The biggest temple in the world. Come for sunrise over the lotus ponds, or later in the day when it is quieter.

items.name: Angkor Thom and Bayon
items.text: The old royal city and the Bayon temple, with more than 200 giant stone faces.

items.name: Ta Prohm
items.text: The jungle temple, with huge tree roots growing over the walls.

items.name: Banteay Srei
items.text: The small pink temple with the finest carvings, about 40 minutes from town.

items.name: Kulen Mountain waterfall (Phnom Kulen)
items.text: The holy mountain: swim at the waterfall and see the river carvings and the big reclining Buddha.

items.name: Beng Mealea
items.text: A wild jungle temple, half fallen down and covered in trees, about 1.5 hours from Siem Reap.

items.name: Tonle Sap floating village
items.text: Houses on stilts and boats on the biggest lake in Southeast Asia.

items.name: Butterfly Paradise
items.text: A tropical garden full of butterflies, with waterfalls, koi ponds and a plant-based café. Learn how a caterpillar becomes a butterfly. [butterflyparadise.net](https://www.butterflyparadise.net/)

items.name: APOPO HeroRATs (landmine rats)
items.text: Meet the giant rats trained to sniff out landmines. Watch a live demonstration and learn how Cambodia clears its minefields. A short drive from town, easy to add after Angkor Wat.

items.name: Angkor Eye
items.text: An 85 m Ferris wheel with air-conditioned cabins. Best at sunset.

items.name: Pub Street and the Night Market
items.text: Food, drinks and shopping in the evening. I drop you off and pick you up.

items.name: Battambang
items.text: A quiet old river town about 3 hours from Siem Reap: the bamboo train, Phnom Sampov mountain and the Bat Caves. I lived there when I was a monk.

faq.q: How far is the new airport?
faq.a: The new airport (SAI) is about 50 km from Siem Reap town. In my van it takes about 1 hour. Send me your flight number and I will watch for delays, so I am there when you land.
My van is a Toyota Alphard. It is cool, quiet and comfortable, with strong air-con and cold water. You can sit back and relax between the temples.
No. My transfer and tour prices are for the whole van, not for each person. Travelling with family or friends? You share one price.

faq.q: How many people and bags fit?
faq.a: My van takes up to 6 guests. With big suitcases, 4 guests is most comfortable. Tell me your group size and bags on WhatsApp, and I will make sure everything fits.

faq.q: Can you guide me inside the temples?
faq.a: Yes. I am a licensed Siem Reap guide, so I can guide you inside the temples too.
It is easy. Send me a WhatsApp message with your dates, how many people and your hotel. I will reply with the price.

faq.q: Do I need an Angkor Pass?
faq.a: Yes, you need an Angkor Pass to visit the temples. You can buy it online before you come, at [angkorenterprise.gov.kh](https://www.angkorenterprise.gov.kh/). Or I can take you to the official ticket office on the way. The pass is not included in the van price.

faq.q: I'm in Bangkok. How do I get to Siem Reap?
faq.a: The easy way now is to fly. The flight from Bangkok is about 1 hour, and I will meet you at SAI airport. Thinking about the land border? Please message me first, and I will tell you the latest.
